content.hook_text: I used to think this verse meant God would give me everything I wanted
content.subtext: Then I read the whole chapter...
content.verse_text: Take delight in the Lord, and he will give you the desires of your heart.
content.misconception: I treated this like a vending machine promise — if I love God enough, He'll hand me the job, the relationship, the life I sketched out.
content.actual_meaning: The Hebrew word for 'delight' (anag) means to be soft, pliable, tender. It's not about performing devotion to get stuff. It's about letting God reshape what you actually want. The desires of your heart *become* His desires — not the other way around.
content.reflection: I journaled this last month and realized I was praying for God to bless my plans instead of asking Him to replace them. The promise isn't 'God gives you what you want.' It's 'God makes you want what He wants to give you.' That's a completely different verse.
content.cta: What verse have you misunderstood? Drop it below 👇
content.caption:
I had Psalm 37:4 on a sticky note for years before I actually read the chapter.

Turns out, it's not about getting what you want. It's about wanting what He gives.

The Hebrew word for 'delight' (anag) means to be soft, pliable — to let God reshape your desires until they match His.

That's way better than a vending machine promise.
